A 60-year-old beekeeper travels across different regions to follow blooming seasons all year round. When inspecting his hives on workdays, he always enjoys recording the variations in honey quality produced from different flower species.

The 25-year-old is a rising singer from a local girl group, who is often spotted practicing her vocals in front of the mirror in the rehearsal room. He is a ride-hailing driver working on the streets of Port-au-Prince, who knows all the routes and fare calculations like the back of his hand. I work the cash register at a Korean grocery store in an old residential neighborhood of Seoul. The 23-year-old guy spends most of his time hanging out in underground electronic music clubs, tweaking equipment and DJing sets. The 20-year-old girl works as a cashier at a community grocery store by the Congo River. In her free time, she scrolls through short videos of Sapeur fashion outfits. A 20-year-old truck driver always runs short-haul routes along the Mekong River in his dust-caked pickup, hauling brocade sacks and fragrant glutinous rice. This is a 70-year-old master carpenter from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. He squats planing wood in his workshop at the edge of the rainforest, his knuckles covered in thin calluses from years of gripping carving knives, always humming rumba tunes half a beat behind. When he calls it a day, he carries a small stool to sit by the door, playing cards with his old pals over palm wine. She is a 31-year-old accountant. Her workstation is stacked with Chinese-Japanese bilingual account books, and an Inari omamori is tucked in the corner of her desk. Her fingertips often carry the faint aroma of ink paste.

A 23-year-old young man works as a waiter at a street food stall on Surabaya Old Street. He is always bustling around with his head down.

This 18-year-old food delivery rider on the streets of Bangkok always remembers to press his palms together in a traditional Thai wai and smile when handing over meals to customers. After finishing his shift, he loves squatting by the roadside to play Thai-style card games with his fellow riders. Even if he gets caught in the rain while rushing to fulfill orders, he will still burst out laughing as he scrolls through funny short videos on his phone.

A 34-year-old woman zips through the streets and alleys of Rio on a chipped motorcycle delivering takeout. She never takes a day off even when heavy rain pounds against her helmet, and always hums capoeira tunes while dropping off orders. After work, she loves squatting at roadside stalls sipping ice-cold beer and scrolling through funny short videos, with a dried carnation forever tucked in her pocket.

A 32-year-old man, whose consulting room is filled with the aroma of yerba mate, often uses the forward and backward steps of tango as a metaphor for interpersonal boundaries. On weekends, he always invites old friends to play bridge in the park, and he grins when he wins.

He is a 33-year-old foreign trade salesman. He always greets clients with a respectful palms-together bow first. She is a 23-year-old itinerant nurse from Papua New Guinea who speaks three tribal dialects. She always dresses wounds for the elderly and children with a warm smile. In her spare time, she gathers with other women from her village to play cards. She also loves collecting mini masks for the local Sing Sing Festival, which she hangs on the side of her medical kit.

He is a 33-year-old dentist, punctual and rigorous. The precision dental instruments in his clinic are always well-polished and neatly organized. On weekends, he always hangs out at the community beer pub, drinking dark beer while playing cards with his old friends.

The 33-year-old CEO of a startup always holds a celadon teacup and expounds on the "philosophy of Confucian merchants" when meeting clients, yet turns around to harshly berate his subordinates the moment the clients leave. The 18-year-old girl is a Chinese-style fashion model who often poses for shoots in the studio. She is an assembly line worker at a food processing plant. She spends all day standing at her station twisting jam jar lids, just going through the motions. This 18-year-old girl works as a model. When in front of the camera, she always fusses over her stray hairs repeatedly under the fill light. A 19-year-old girl works as a tea artisan at a tiny corner teahouse. Her wrist twists gently when she brews tea. She always secretly drinks any improperly brewed tea, saying that no one should let the tea leaves' efforts go to waste.

A Kenyan man in his seventies drives a beat-up sedan to provide ride-hailing services on the outskirts of the city. A 19-year-old girl working at an e-commerce customer service center in London always answers every call in a soft, warm tone, and gently tidies up her headphone cord after hanging up. A 24-year-old young man mans the sentry booth of a residential community. After getting home from work, he always brews himself a cup of chaoqing (roasted green tea) and sips it slowly while watching short food videos.

The 32-year-old agricultural expert shuttles between various plantations. When guiding farmers, she always taps her notebook with a sharpened pencil, speaking in a tone that brooks no dissent. After work, she loves to drag the old hands at the plantation to play local card games, and always stays up late scrolling through short videos about coffee cultivation before going to bed.

A 27-year-old male doctor works at a clinic on the fringes of the grasslands. He always keeps his stethoscope firmly slung around the left side of his neck. After work, he stays cooped up in his yurt dorm scrolling through short videos of nomadic delicacies, and the only thing he does outside of this routine is hand milk candies to children from the pastoral areas.

She is a female CEO in the petroleum industry. On workdays, she handles projects in her office with traditional Caucasian woven carpets covering the floor. In her leisure time, she enjoys listening to Muqam records and has long been an avid collector of vintage oil exploration badges. She is known for her decisiveness in everything she does.

On a small farm along the Mississippi River, the 18-year-old girl is always bent over tending to soybeans, humming the little blues ditty her grandmother taught her as she works. In the evenings, she huddles in the old trailer scrolling through short videos of farm makeovers. Even when the harvest is dismal, she never forgets to save half a piece of cornbread for her old yellow dog.

An 18-year-old girl works as a caregiver for a diaspora family in Mombasa. Every day, she wipes down furniture crusted with sea salt from the ocean breeze and helps turn the bedridden elderly member of the household over. After getting off work, she always squats at the alley entrance scrolling through funny short videos. She loves stashing away the candies given by her employer, and hums the religious ballads she has listened to since childhood all the while doing her chores.

A 26-year-old young woman rides an electric delivery bike with chipped paint, weaving through old alleyways to deliver parcels. She carries a palm-sized tea canister with her, and sips strong tea to fight fatigue when taking breaks. After work, she always joins the crowd playing Doudizhu (a popular Chinese card game) downstairs in her residential community, and buys a popsicle for herself whenever she loses.

He is a plumber and electrician working in a residential neighborhood in Brazil, with his fingertips always smudged with indelible copper rust. Every day, he climbs up and down stairs with a tool bag slung over his shoulder, fixing water pipes and running electrical wiring. After work, he likes nothing better than to squat on the sidewalk with a bottle of iced cachaça, watching samba troupes rehearse. On weekends, he also drops by the community capoeira trial class to get half an hour of free warm-up practice in.

A 34-year-old woman sells replica models of Aksum stone carvings and rock-hewn churches at a souvenir shop in the old town of Addis Ababa. After work, she loves hunkering down in her rented apartment to binge-watch local soap operas. She always keeps a small rock fragment from her hometown in her pocket, and even when customers haggle the price down to the point where she only makes a meager profit, she can hardly bring herself to say "no".

A 32-year-old woman works as a teacher at an adobe classroom on the edge of a tribal area in Papua New Guinea. Every day she grips a piece of chalk to teach local children Austronesian dialects, with half a Sing Sing Festival mask tucked away in her drawer as a teaching aid.
During classes, she always asks the strongest kid to carry water for her. After school, her favorite pastime is squatting under the eaves playing cards. She always licks her lower lip before playing a card, and only lays her card down once she has a full grasp of her opponents' playing patterns.

He is a 72-year-old agricultural expert from Nigeria. He always keeps an indigo-dyed cloth handkerchief on hand to wipe sweat, and has spent most of his life out in the fields researching drought-resistant crops to help villagers boost their incomes. When he has free time, he loves to round up his fellow townsfolk to play cards together under the coconut trees.

A 27-year-old Thai young man works as an accountant at a grocery trading firm in Chinatown. When vendors come to press for pending payments, he can only clutch his calculator, purse his lips and dare not make a sound, with his fingertips always stained with ink pad smudges. After work, his favorite pastime is squatting by street stalls, gnawing on charcoal-grilled pork jowl, washing it down with iced beer while binge-watching Chinese historical costume dramas. Whenever he makes an accounting mistake, he habitually bites through the rubber cover of the pen cap.

Next to the ancient ruins of the old city of Samarkand, the figure of a young girl is a familiar sight. The 20-year-old works as a local tour guide. When explaining the history of Timur's Mausoleum, she occasionally fumbles for words, blushing and scratching the back of her head. After work, she always meets up with fellow locals to squat by the street and enjoy grilled skewers. In her free time, she loves joining casual sessions of local card games. She always carries pilaf balls made by her mother in her pocket, and hands one to any tourist who looks worn out.

She is a food delivery rider working the streets of Cotonou. Quiet and reserved, she curls up in her rental apartment binging Nigerian soap operas as soon as she finishes her shift. She always shows up five minutes ahead of schedule for every delivery and is never late.

A 31-year-old farm woman grows quinoa every day on the field ridges where a mix of Spanish and indigenous farming techniques is practiced. When she calls it a day at dusk, she carries a low stool to play cards with her neighbors. Even if she loses, she slaps her thigh and laughs, humming folk tunes under her breath.

He is 28 years old. As a civil servant in New Zealand, he usually coordinates affairs related to the promotion of marine culture at the assembly hall on workdays. After work, he always likes to shoulder his fishing tackle and go fishing by the shore. In his spare time, he also practices the haka with the elders.

He is a 32-year-old CEO of a cultural and creative company dedicated to supporting creators. On workdays, he spends most of his time sorting out project plans in his office stacked with vinyl records. In his spare time, he loves hanging out at neighborhood jazz bars and often organizes Texas Hold'em games with his subordinates. No one in the whole company sees him as a distant, unapproachable boss.

At 35, he runs a vintage barbershop on a street corner in Brooklyn. The walls are adorned with tiny Stars and Stripes trinkets and old Western movie posters.
He cuts hair with sharp, precise movements, never chasing the latest Hollywood fads — he only relies on his well-practiced touch to pick a style that fits each client's face shape. During his downtime, he plays Texas Hold'em with regulars, and he never misses his weekly Saturday fishing trip to the suburbs. He always takes extra care to trim his customers' sideburns perfectly neat and even.

The 33-year-old flight attendant has a voice as soft as the trailing note of a blues ballad when she serves meals at work. When off duty, she loves curling up in her rented apartment binging old civil rights-themed dramas, and she always saves leftover milk candies from passengers to give to the kids at the community church.

She is a 33-year-old primary school teacher in Indonesia. In her spare time after school, she teaches children to play angklung, a local traditional bamboo musical instrument. When she is free, she curls up on the balcony of her bamboo house binge-watching local family dramas. She always wears a soft, faint smile when interacting with others.

As a caregiver, she tends to the elderly residents of the apartment gently and quietly every day. During the New Potato Festival, she slips homemade steamed potato cakes to the seniors she is familiar with. After work, she binge-watches family dramas; on weekends, she rounds up fellow townsfolk to play cards. When she is worn out, she rubs the spot behind her ear and hums little folk tunes from her hometown.

The yoga and Pilates instructor, who just turned 18, always patiently corrects students' movements with improper muscle engagement. They carry a glass jar of brewed aged white tea with them at all times, and often invite familiar regular students to play a few rounds of mahjong after class. Though a person of few words, they can always pick up on others' emotions with perfect accuracy.

He is a 28-year-old frontline municipal civil servant. He sits at the service window against bright yellow painted walls, issuing all kinds of certificates for local residents at a leisurely pace. After work, he often invites friends to play casual pickup five-a-side football. In his spare time, he scrolls through short videos of previous carnival parades to kill time.

This 29-year-old model often struts down the runway to the rhythm of Muqam, or shoots fashion spreads featuring Western Regions-style outfits in the studio. After wrapping up work for the day, she always loves meeting up with her childhood friends for red willow-grilled lamb skewers, and scrolling through short-form videos of food spot reviews.

This 19-year-old guy works on grain transport routes across the black soil regions. When he stops for a rest, he either hangs out with fellow drivers to play poker, or scrolls through short videos about Eastern Orthodox folk customs to pass the time.

She is a female painter over 50, who often spends her days in her small riverside studio tracing the soft satin patterns of ao dai and the vibrant paint on water puppets. In her free time, she can often be found huddled over a bowl of fresh rice noodles binging local family dramas. She always weaves subtle Confucian cultural imagery into her creations, and no one can ever guess the clever core concept behind her next work.

The 34-year-old female journalist always weaves through the old neighborhoods of Havana with a voice recorder in hand. She stakes out sites to record the chants of Santería rituals and the African drumbeats of rumba troupes, and a half-finished cup of black coffee spiked with rum always sits open beside her manuscripts.
After work, she loves nothing more than curling up in her rental apartment binging Latin American telenovelas. When she runs into ridiculously cheesy plotlines, she slaps the couch and laughs so hard she chokes. While revising her drafts, she unconsciously chews on the rubber sleeve of her pen cap.

As an insurance salesman with two decades of experience in the industry, he tramps from street to street with frayed insurance application forms tucked under his arm. When it comes to calculating rebates, he won't yield a single cent. In his free time, he either hunts for near-expiry Bordeaux wine to enjoy alone, or pops round to his neighbors' to play bridge, and only pulls out the mints he carries with him to give away two pieces after he wins a game.

She runs a small stall alongside Barkhor Street, selling homemade butter flower pendants and mini prayer wheels. A hard worker who never complains about hardship, she loves squatting at the entrance of her stall scrolling through short Tibetan-language lifestyle videos after closing up for the day. When she bumps into fellow vendors she knows well, she will also join them for a couple of rounds of poker.

A 26-year-old British female influencer livestreams from her cozy sunlit apartment every day, teaching her fans how to dance carnival steps. Off camera, she loves binge-watching over-the-top dramatic British shows, and makes a point of meeting up with friends to play Texas Hold'em every weekend.

She is a 21-year-old assembly line worker at an electronics factory on the outskirts of Bangkok. Whenever she meets others, she always gives an awkward traditional Thai greeting, pressing her palms together and bowing her head.

She works a full 10 hours a day inserting electronic components, leaving stubborn solder stains between her fingers that never wash off. After work, she holes up in her rented apartment scrolling through short clips of Thai dramas. She has been saving up her pocket money, waiting for Loy Krathong to release a banana-leaf water lantern by the river.

At 3 p.m. sharp, she always lays out a proper English afternoon tea in her small kitchen. After retiring, she plays bridge at the community center every Wednesday. Most of the ditsy floral bone china teaspoons in her collection are old stock from her father's factory in Birmingham. Even if she burns the scones, she just shrugs it off, and she always makes a point of placing the sugar jar at a precise 45-degree angle.

She is a 34-year-old Argentine woman who runs a hand-knitting stall on a street corner. Her Andean-style alpaca wool scarves and coasters are all neatly displayed. When someone tries to haggle unreasonably, she will snap back unapologetically, only to quietly slip a tiny handwoven charm as a freebie to the customer afterward. After wrapping up her stall each day, she always squats by the curb scrolling through funny Latin American short videos. On weekends, she loves gathering with the girls from neighboring stalls to play card games.

A 20-year-old guy works the sentry booth at a tech park. No one without an access card can sneak into the building when he's on duty, no exceptions. When he finishes his shift, he brews himself a cup of cheap Tieguanyin and sips it like a total pro. After work, he always drags his fellow guards on the same post to the alley mouth to grab grilled skewers and scroll through short videos.

In a small teahouse where tables are draped with brushed linen tablecloths, a 37-year-old woman curls up behind the bar, kneading and twisting yerba mate stalks. She always draws her shoulders in slightly when handing mate cups to customers.

On her days off, she holes up in her rented apartment binging Latin American telenovelas, collects patterned teabag wrappers to press between the pages of a well-worn dictionary, and occasionally taps her foot to tango tunes—only to freeze up immediately the moment someone catches her in the act.

A 23-year-old youth tends to a cramped little tea shop next to the old port of Dar es Salaam. He always carefully wipes his copper pot adorned with Arab motifs three times before brewing tea. After closing up shop at dusk, he likes to squat on the stone steps playing cards with his neighbors, and often zones out staring at the single-masted dhows returning to the harbour.

She runs a tiny nail salon in the narrow alleys of Seville. When working on clients' nails, she always hums little flamenco tunes, and loves decorating their nails with patterns inspired by flamenco dress hems. In her free time, she munches on tapas while binge-watching local comedy shows, and on weekends she often drops by the neighborhood dance club to dance flamenco.

She is a woman who has worked in customer service in Brazil for six years. Every day, she clutches an overheated headset to handle inquiries for eight straight hours, leaving her voice constantly hoarse. After work, she curls up in her rental apartment scrolling through short clips of capoeira matches, and on weekends she occasionally drops by neighborhood samba gatherings to join in the fun.

The 19-year-old young man appears in Tokyo’s old neighborhoods pushing a street sweeper long before dawn. Meticulous in every task, he even carefully picks up the tattered paper gohei (Shinto ritual streamers) next to shrine torii gates, with a distinct bushido-style earnestness about him. After work, he always ducks into an izakaya for grilled skewers and iced beer, and saves up to collect Showa-era samurai-themed anime cassettes.

He is a 34-year-old sanitation worker in charge of cleaning the streets and alleys of the old town. When sweeping the streets, he always casually hums snippets of Muqam tunes. After work, there is nothing he enjoys more than squatting at the alley entrance to play a couple of rounds of Dou Dizhu with his fellow workers. When the evening breeze drifts by carrying the savory aroma of roasted naan, he always breaks into a warm grin.

A 34-year-old photographer spends all year roaming the grasslands. He always chases the horse races at the Nadam Fair and the lingering melodies of the morin khuur to photograph yurts at dawn and dusk. If he fails to capture the satisfying soft light he is after, he will squat on the meadow and sulk. In his spare time, he loves nothing more than joining local herders for a poker game.

A 32-year-old woman runs a tiny wedding studio in a small town along the Pacific coast. She always likes incorporating traditional drum beats into wedding arrangements. After work, she curls up at home binging Latin American soap operas. On weekends, she meets up with her besties for grilled skewers paired with corn wine. When working on wedding plans, she always unconsciously twists the mint tin in her hand.

The 49-year-old researcher spends all day in his lab piled high with rubbings of stone crosses and lettered manuscripts. When lost in thought, he always fumbles with the tiny repatriated stone cross left by his grandfather that he keeps in his pocket. Every Friday, without fail, he heads to the tavern at the alley entrance with his colleagues for homemade pomegranate wine. He also loves scrolling through short archaeology videos to unwind in his spare time.

This is a veteran singer from the Republic of the Congo. His singing carries the surge of the Congo River's waves. He loves fishing by the riverbank at dusk, and never misses his weekly card games with his old pals on weekends. Whenever he loses, he hums little tunes he composed himself.

As a high-speed rail attendant in Peru, she always helps passengers stow their luggage and check tickets, while her fingertips often brush against the Catholic medallion in her pocket. After work, she curls up in her rental apartment to binge-watch family dramas, and she loves making ceviche at home on weekends.

In the old markets of Buenos Aires, he spends his days weaving through the crowds with stacks of Andean woven blankets slung over his shoulders. The thick calluses on his knuckles are flecked with colored threads rubbed off from the braiding ropes he works with. When his shift ends, he always squats on the street corner to play cards with his fellow workers. If he wins, he treats himself to a cup of mate and sips it leisurely. Whenever he meets a new coworker, he always tucks a small hand-braided knot into their hand as a welcome gift.

She is a 26-year-old beekeeper from Guatemala. She looks after her beehives in the wooded hills next to the cornfields. After calling it a day, she squats at the village entrance playing poker with her female fellow villagers, always with half a piece of warm corn tucked in her pocket.

This 33-year-old preschool teacher spends her days in a classroom filled with mbiras and mini stone carvings, soothing children with ancient nursery rhymes. Every now and then, she hides the colorful candies and tells the kids they were carried off by the sacred birds of Great Zimbabwe.

As soon as she gets off work, she dives straight for the card stall at the alley entrance. When she wins, she treats herself to roasted corn, and she always loves weaving the corn silk into tiny rings to slip onto her fingers.

The 32-year-old designer runs a small loft studio in Dublin's old town, where he prints Celtic knot patterns and short Gaelic phrases on canvas bags. Most of his inspiration comes from the oral epics his grandmother told him when he was little. Every Wednesday after work, he always stops by the corner bar for a game of cards, with lemon throat lozenges permanently tucked in his pocket.

He is a 21-year-old young man from Zimbabwe. For years, he has worked as a fisherman casting nets for fish on the banks of the Zambezi River. After work, he either squats at the foot of the colorful mural wall of his house to play cards with his neighbors, or scrolls through short videos.

He is a 35-year-old fisherman from the east coast of Canada. Most days, he goes out fishing on his small boat in the waters off Newfoundland. During the closed fishing season, he either plays ice hockey at the community center, or hangs out with his fellow townsfolk to play cards at the small tavern on the dock.

After retirement, he would always carry a bamboo chair to the veranda of his family's bamboo stilt house to play cards with his old pals. In his free time, he brews glutinous rice-flavored tea. Whenever anyone asks him about old anecdotes from the Water Splashing Festival, he always answers cheerfully with a warm grin.

The 36-year-old man runs a cut fruit stall at the entrance of an old alley in Kashgar. Whenever customers bargain with him, he readily gives in without hesitation. When he is free, he squats by his stall scrolling through short videos of Muqam performances, and occasionally plays a couple of rounds of poker with vendors at neighboring stalls. When closing up for the day, he always sweeps the surrounding area spotlessly clean, never daring to cause the slightest trouble for others.

He is a lawyer based in the Brazilian Amazon, who has devoted three decades to advocating for land rights in the rainforest. A vine totem woven by his mother hangs on his office wall, and he always rubs the palm seed his grandfather gave him, which he keeps in his pocket, before every court hearing. After work, he loves lingering at the small bistro on the street corner over an ice-cold beer. On weekends, he goes catfish fishing with his old pals, and he has impeccable sportsmanship when playing cards — he never gets worked up no matter how the game goes.

The 22-year-old young man huddles in a cubicle at an esports club in Tokyo, his fingertips tapping furiously fast on the keyboard. During training breaks, he loves squatting in the hallway scrolling through short anime clips and playing Japanese hanafuda. On off-season days, he heads alone to the izakaya at the end of the alley to enjoy grilled skewers paired with warm sake.

This girl from Eritrea, who just turned twenty, incorporates Aksum stone carving patterns, Christian crosses and Islamic crescent-and-star elements into her cultural and creative designs at a small studio. When she gets stuck revising her drafts, she pouts and plucks at the edges of her rough sketches. Every night like clockwork, she binges on cheesy over-the-top sweet romance dramas, always nibbling on a half-eaten date scone as she watches.

She is a 31-year-old fitness instructor. When teaching group fitness classes, she always subconsciously clutches a half bottle of disinfectant spray, for fear that her trainees will use too much and waste it. When she is free, she loves nothing more than popping into the tiny bistro at the alley entrance to play bridge. She occasionally hums a few lines of flamenco tunes along with the background music, and always picks the most budget-friendly paella set on the menu.

As a Japanese-style pattern designer, he works energetically in his studio stacked with washi paper sketches, with his fingers flitting rapidly across the graphics tablet. He always gives his bushido-themed keychain a quick tap before revising any draft. After work, he loves dragging his colleagues to izakayas for grilled skewers, sipping cold beer while scrolling through short anime videos for inspiration.

The 27-year-old woman is a fund manager at an investment bank. On workdays, she stares at candlestick charts and pores over financial reports, and her well-honed sense of propriety bears the deep imprint of Confucian influence. On weekends, she curls up at home binging suspense dramas, has a cute little quirk of biting pen caps, and always keeps a warm cup of Keemun black tea within arm's reach.

A 30-year-old man has spent seven years staring at candlestick charts in the investment bank office building adjacent to Prague's Old Town. When calculating trading commissions, he always unconsciously taps his fingertips on the desk. After work, he loves popping into small taverns tucked away in alleyways for an icy Pilsner, and plays Texas Hold'em with his poker buddies on a fixed schedule every Friday.

75-year-old male fruit grower, a veteran kiwifruit farmer who has grown kiwifruit in the Qinling Mountains of Shaanxi for 50 years. When he was young, he stayed in the mountains for three straight days and nights to guard his kiwifruit orchard and fend off wild boars. He flatly refuses to use chemical fertilizers, insisting on applying rotten leaves and sheep manure instead. "Kiwifruit trees take root in the soil, so they must be nurtured the old way. How can we recklessly change that?" he says. Every day after finishing work, he squats at the entrance of his courtyard to feed his fighting cocks, whose cage is woven from kiwifruit vines.

The 18-year-old female model regularly shoots Guo Feng (Chinese traditional aesthetic style) themed sample shots. After wrapping up her work for the day, she always loves to brew a pot of Gongfu tea, curl up on the small sofa in her rental apartment, and binge-watch ancient Chinese costume dramas centered on political intrigue. It is only when the conversation turns to the tea ceremony that her eyes light up with great excitement.

A 23-year-old young man, he is a lawyer who has only been in the profession for half a year. At the law firm, he stays in his cubicle, always buried in towering stacks of case files. His fingers tap the keyboard steadily and swiftly, and he speaks in a slow, mild tone yet with perfectly airtight logic. After work, he curls up in his rental apartment binge-watching historical costume dramas centered on political intrigue. There is always a warm cup of aged tea on the corner of his desk, and he loves sorting his collected tea bags by category, with all the labels written neatly and immaculately.

A 32-year-old man has worked as a food delivery rider for years, braving the elements day in and day out. He is always punctual with every single delivery. When he has spare time, he loves stopping by the old pub near his home for a glass of iced beer, and occasionally joins a casual group to play a few rounds of local poker.

The 18-year-old girl works as a tour guide. When she shows visitors around Gamla Stan, Stockholm's old town, she recounts Viking legends in a soft voice and never rambles unnecessarily. In her free time, her favorite pastime is putting together minimalist Viking-themed jigsaw puzzles. She always saves up her days off for Midsummer to pick wild berries in the countryside.

The 31-year-old professor gives lectures in an office stacked with cowhide-bound ancient books. A carved wooden longhorn statue sits by the podium, and he occasionally performs a simplified version of war dance during classes. After work, he scrolls through short videos of wild animals. On weekends, he hangs out with his colleagues for grilled skewers and beer, and he often stays up late into the night preparing lessons. He is a man of few words and speaks at a slow, unhurried pace.

The night security guard at an office building in Dublin's Old Town can never resist sneaking peeks at female white-collar workers heading home late. While on duty, he always props his feet up on the monitoring console, huddles over his phone to play Dou Dizhu (a popular three-player Chinese card game) via video call with his card-playing pals. He keeps a half-drunk bottle of Guinness stashed in his drawer, and whenever he loses a round, he hums a few lines of old Gaelic tunes he only half understands. He always makes a furtive sign of the cross before starting his shift.

This 47-year-old nurse gently soothes patients in the minimalist ward. She always keeps homemade gingerbread in her pocket to hand out to fussy little patients. After work, she loves binge-watching series adapted from fairy tales, and goes to a small bistro with her besties for hot apple cider every Friday without fail, weaving the laid-back, cozy Hygge vibe into every bit of her daily life.

A 44-year-old female photographer, carrying her old film camera, wanders through the streets of Havana, capturing shots of bright yellow vintage cars, salsa dancers and cigar artisans. After work, she always stops by the small eatery at the alley entrance for a mojito, plays dominoes with the local folks, and always has half a piece of coconut candy tucked in her pocket.

A 26-year-old woman runs a hand-pulled noodle shop in the Kathmandu foothills. Even when the scorching midday sun makes beads of sweat drip down her forehead, she never pauses kneading the dough. With quick, deft flicks of her wrists, evenly sized hand-pulled noodles drop into the boiling broth. After closing up shop for the day, she usually scrolls through short videos posted by mountaineering vloggers, or plays a few rounds of cards with her neighbors.

As a nurse at a community hospital in Osaka, she shuttles between wards every day and writes medical records in neat Chinese characters. Before her shift starts, she always clasps her palms together in silent prayer at the small shrine in the hospital's backyard. After work, her favorite thing to do is curl up in her rental apartment to binge-watch hot-blooded anime. She always keeps mints in her pocket to soothe crying little patients.

The 33-year-old female farmer spends all day tending to her cassava crops in the red soil at the edge of the East African savannah. She loves nothing more than squatting at the foot of the adobe wall at dusk playing cards with her neighbors. When nobody's looking, she will secretly stand on tiptoe and dance a few steps of the jumping dance.

He runs a small minimalist shop, with wooden hooks decorated with replicated Viking motifs mounted on the walls. He always hums old folk tunes while grooming cats and dogs. After work, he squats at the entrance of the shop scrolling through short pet videos. He loves inviting friends out for cold beer during the Midsummer Festival, and always grooms stray cats for free whenever he runs into them.

As a reporter covering the culture beat, I often tote a camera shuttling between stables, carpet workshops and oasis villages. In my spare time, my favorite pastime is scrolling through short folklore videos, and I also have the habit of collecting carpet scraps with different patterns to use as bookmarks.

The 35-year-old man works as a security guard in Tokyo's commercial district. While on duty, he always helps elderly people carry heavy items. After work, he invariably heads to an izakaya for grilled skewers and iced beer. On his days off, he slings a fishing rod over his shoulder and spends the entire afternoon sitting by the river. He has been immersed in martial arts culture since childhood.

The 21-year-old is an up-and-coming independent singer. He spends most of his time rehearsing in an old Gothic building converted into a rehearsal studio. In his free time, he loves collecting vintage postcards of historic architecture. Once he wraps up his work for the day, he always invites friends to the pub for freshly brewed dark beer. He is never even a second late for any appointment.

As a Colombian female writer, she lives in a small cabin on the edge of the rainforest writing stories of her people. In her free time, she loves binge-watching over-the-top Latin American telenovelas, and collects uniquely shaped rainforest leaf vein specimens.

This 34-year-old clerk always sorts and files documents at her desk in line with the classification logic of the Jiada System on a daily basis. She is a huge fan of local family dramas, and has stashed more than a dozen cow-shaped pottery ornaments picked up from local fairs in her drawer. When she has spare time, she would gently rub these ornaments with her fingertips and stare off into space lost in thought.

As a journalist, she often spends long hours staking out North Sea oil platforms and Viking ruins along the fjords to cover stories. In her private life, her favorite pastime is playing bridge online with old colleagues every Wednesday. She takes a sip of light beer whenever she wins a game, and always keeps dried salted cod in her pocket as a snack.

When this 25-year-old young American takes a seat at his workstation in a Silicon Valley startup campus, he vanishes into the sea of people in the blink of an eye. As the CEO of a startup, the very air grows tense when he scans through financing reports. A firm believer in Silicon Valley's ethos of innovation and individual striving, he always orders his Americano with triple espresso shots. His only weekly reprieve is playing Texas Hold 'em with friends every Friday night. He flips poker chips between his fingertips far more deftly than he twirls a pen during board meetings. If he loses, he just presses his lips into a thin line, and turns right around to mull over product iterations.

A 21-year-old guy spends most of his time holed up in a tiny studio packed with audio mixing gear, creating Chinese-style electronic music. He often rummages through ancient Chinese classics for inspiration, and always invites friends to savor tea together in his free time. Before stepping on stage for a DJ set, he will touch the portable tea bag in his pocket first, otherwise he won't feel reassured at all.

A male lawyer with only two years of practice under his belt, he speaks in a soft, gentle tone. He often totes a notebook embroidered with Zhuang brocade patterns to stilt-house villages to carry out legal literacy education and mediation work. A tiny bronze drum figurine sits beside his case files all the time. In his leisure time, he loves heading to Zhuang song fairs to listen to mountain folk songs, and on weekends he always invites his colleagues out to grab grilled skewers and iced beer at the alley entrance.

The 29-year-old woman is a reggae singer who often performs on small open-air stages in Kingston. She has a clear, crisp singing voice, loves competing in sprints with her neighbors in her spare time, and has collected an entire cabinet full of old reggae vinyl records.

After retiring, he settles in a minimalist log cabin by the lake. He gets up every morning to polish his collection of Viking wood carvings. Every Wednesday without fail, he squeezes into the neighborhood pub with his old pals, sipping cider paired with pickled herring. He always hums old Midsummer tunes, and never fails to have mints in his pocket to amuse passing children.

She is the most popular service window clerk at the government service hall. At 23, she has just landed a civil service post after passing the exam, and never loses her temper even when she has to answer the same question ten times in a row. After work, she curls up in her rented apartment, brews a cup of Tieguanyin tea, and leisurely whiles away the time watching the latest episodes of a family ethics drama.

The 32-year-old works as a high-speed rail attendant in Argentina. When conducting ticket checks, a quick sidelong glance is all it takes for her to catch fare dodgers trying to sneak past without paying. On her days off, she either dances tango at the local community club, or hangs out with friends over grilled ribs at a small backyard gathering.

She is a 30-year-old professional organizer. She always hums marimba tunes from her hometown while tidying up. In her spare time, her favorite pastime is binge-watching Latin American telenovelas. On weekends, she invites her neighbors to play cards at the alley entrance, and even when she loses, she laughs openly and heartily.

A 34-year-old woman runs a small pet grooming shop in an old neighborhood. Every day she squats on the floor trimming fur and clipping nails for cats and dogs. When her back gets sore, she gives it a couple of thumps and carries on with her work. After closing up for the day, she always heads to the foot of the Bagan-style pagoda replica at the street corner, where she joins the neighbors for a card game and simply laughs whenever she loses.

A 33-year-old woman teaches Pilates at a small studio in the old quarter of Istanbul, where the floor is covered with a family-heirloom Ottoman jacquard carpet. She speaks in a soft, gentle tone during classes, giving her students light pats on the back when correcting their movements.
After class, she curls up on the sofa binge-watching Turkish TV dramas. Every Wednesday, she invites her best friends over to brew Turkish coffee, and they play the Chinese card game *Shengji* (also known as Tractor) as they sip their drinks. Whenever she loses, she pouts and tugs at the tassels of the carpet. She leads a really steady, fulfilling life.

The 30-year-old barista runs a small seaside shop on Mindanao. With light brown coffee stains on his hands, he smiles as he hands over a cappuccino sprinkled with shredded coconut. In his spare time, he keeps up with local soap operas, and invites neighbors to play cards right after work. On rainy days, he always hums Austronesian fishing songs, and brews every cup of coffee warm and cozy.

This 45-year-old female designer has her studio strewn with home furnishing drafts that integrate nomadic patterns with modern aesthetics. She is extremely meticulous about her work. After work, nothing beats curling up on the carpet and scrolling through short food videos for her, and she never forgets to stash a few chewy date candies in her drawer as little treats.

Having spent three years working behind a bank counter, they are deft and steady at typing and counting cash. Though quiet by nature, they always solve problems with perfect accuracy. Every day before their shift starts, they make a cup of warm white tea and set it down in the corner of the counter. After work, they curl up on the sofa to binge family dramas, always popping orange gummies into their mouth as they watch.

A 69-year-old female designer works out of a tiny studio stacked with sketches of adobe patterns, weaving the legacy of the Mali Empire and symbols from griot epics into her creations. Every Wednesday evening, she dances adapted West African square dances with her long-time female friends. Before starting each design, she always touches the broken adobe fragment from an ancient mosque that sits on her windowsill.

A 24-year-old guy mans a Halal grill at the night market, flipping meat skewers with sharp, smooth moves. Anyone who nags him about their order gets a glare. When he's got free time, he either rounds up a group of his fellow townsfolk to play cards, or casually hums snippets of *Manas*.

He is a 35-year-old man who has been working freight routes across the Eurasian Steppe for years. He always clutches his phone scrolling for cargo supply leads. When he pulls over for a break, he loves popping over to the service area station to play cards with fellow drivers, and when he has some downtime, he will fish out the small dombra he carries with him and play a few short tunes.

He runs a bustling little barbershop in the old quarter of Copenhagen. He loves humming old tunes from Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales while cutting hair, and the shop walls are studded with the Viking metal badges he has collected over the years. After work, he washes down pickled herring with light lager, joins his neighbors for card games, and always sneaks leftover warm cookies from customers into his pocket.

In the security booth of the underground parking garage of an office building in Gangnam District, Seoul, a 22-year-old South Korean security guard is verifying access for incoming and outgoing vehicles. He never budges no matter how much drivers trying to poach free parking spots sweet-talk and pester him. After his shift, he always squats beside the booth scrolling through K-pop short videos, munching on budae jjigae rice balls paired with spicy kimchi soup.

This 86-year-old retiree spent the first half of his life tending to golden wheat fields. Now, every morning, he brings a cup of turmeric chai to the community pavilion to play cards with his old pals. Even when he loses, he just smiles and pushes his chips across the table, swinging his legs leisurely while humming a soft Punjabi tune. He always tucks a polished wheat kernel in his pocket — that is his most treasured memento.

At 30, she has worked in the pharmacy of a community hospital for five years. Her fingertips always carry a faint, mixed scent of disinfectant and processed Chinese herbal slices. She leaves no room for error even with decimal points when verifying prescriptions, and the herbal slices in the medicine cabinets are arranged perfectly in order of the stroke count of their Chinese names.
After work, she curls up in the rattan chair in her rental apartment, brews a cup of warm Pu'er tea and scrolls through short costume drama clips. Every Wednesday, without fail, she goes to the chess and card room at the alley entrance to play two rounds of mahjong. Even if she loses, she will hand tangerines to the winner.

The 32-year-old engineer has spent years working on irrigation projects in desert oases, and never loses his cool even when the construction schedule is extremely tight. After calling it a day, his favorite pastime is scrolling through folk-themed short videos about carpet weaving, and he occasionally joins his colleagues for a game of local traditional poker.

This 22-year-old young woman works as a model. She often shoots commercials themed around Thai cuisine and the Loy Krathong Festival. After only half an hour of shooting, she will sneak off to the break room to binge-watch Thai dramas, holding an iced coconut juice the whole time while complaining that the fill lights give off so much heat that her skin feels burning hot.

A 26-year-old female farmer. She shuttles between barley fields and berry sheds every day, and picks only minimalist designs for all her farm tools. A thrifted mini iron Viking ship ornament hangs on the wall of her cottage.
In her free time, she enjoys playing cards with neighbors in the barn. On rainy days, she curls up by the warm stove to binge-watch family dramas. There is always a piece of honey candy passed down from her grandma in her pocket, and she says chewing it makes her feel grounded.

He is a 53-year-old dentist. A wooden plaque with unique lettering hangs on the wall of his clinic. He always hums polyphonic tunes from his hometown at work, with a touch as gentle as caressing grapevines. On weekends, he loves gathering with old pals to play bridge. After drinking his homemade red wine, he walks home singing merrily all the way, never letting work weariness linger past sunset.

The 23-year-old woman works as a preschool teacher at a small kindergarten in a residential neighborhood. When soothing crying children, she always clutches her sleeve cuffs and speaks in a soft, quiet voice, rarely lifting her head to meet their eyes. After work, she curls up in her rented apartment binging anime, and on weekends, she occasionally follows free tutorials to learn how to make simple ikebana decorative pieces.

The 21-year-old woman works as a preschool teacher at a kindergarten in the Paris suburbs. She often tells West African oral folktales to the children, and her favorite leisure activity is scrolling through short videos showing the daily lives of West African immigrants. She also hand-weaves small colorful string bracelets as rewards for the kids, and always speaks in a soft, gentle tone.

As a 34-year-old model, she always huddles in a corner backstage when waiting for her cue. In her free time, her favorite pastime is hunting for vintage woven and embroidered patches. Once she wraps up work, she curls up in her apartment binging French family comedies.

This 34-year-old guy always totes his frayed camera bag around, squatting by the banks of the Mekong River, chasing shots of the fingertips of elderly brocade-weaving women and the rolling "waves" of glutinous rice being raked over on the grain drying yard. After finishing his work, he loves to squat at the village entrance and play Lao card games with the local folks.

A 23-year-old woman works on the coastal high-speed railway jointly built by China and Mozambique, where she handles all passengers' needs thoughtfully and appropriately. When off duty, she always likes to invite her fellow townsfolk to play poker, and she keeps a saved playlist of marimba music on her mobile device wherever she goes.

A 25-year-old guy runs a small pet grooming shop in the residential community. He always responds to all customers' requests in a soft, gentle voice, with fine bits of cat and dog fur perpetually stuck to his clothes. When he has free time, he enjoys playing a few tunes on the dombra, and after work he always invites his fellow hometown pals to the alley entrance for grilled skewers and iced beer.

He is a 32-year-old man who works as a cashier at a small-town grocery store. He always gives the wrong change, and crumpled candy wrappers pile up on his checkout counter. After work, he squats by the soft dark soil outside the store entrance, playing cards and drinking cheap beer with his fellow workers, and occasionally humming off-key snippets of Cossack folk songs.

The 23-year-old real estate agent always clutches the corner of his property brochure and dares not lift his gaze when taking clients to view houses. After work, he heads straight back to his rental apartment, cracks open a bottle of affordable Bordeaux, curls up on the sofa and binges old comedy films to enjoy some undisturbed quiet time.

In a tiny coffee shop tucked away in the old alleys of Lhasa, a 29-year-old female barista is brewing coffee. She often takes the chance when turning around to grab the sugar jar to slip near-expiry cookies into the sets for her regulars. Once off work, she heads straight for the teahouse at the alley entrance to play mahjong. Whenever she loses a round, she pouts and mulls over her playing tactics.

The 31-year-old Cameroonian female teacher tends a small classroom on the edge of the rainforest, where she teaches children to master three languages. Her features only soften when she watches short videos to learn traditional mask dances, and she always secretly slips the dried mangoes she has saved up to her timid students.

At 23, she works as an instructor at a community yoga studio. When coaching her students, she always says the same line: "You can only find the right points to engage your muscles when you calm your mind." Before each class, she carefully wipes every yoga block clean with a cotton cloth.

After class, she curls up in a corner of the studio, brews warm tea in a celadon cup, and binges two episodes of a historical power-play drama. Occasionally, she asks the studio owner to join her for a few rounds of mahjong. Her life is steady, grounded and deeply satisfying.

This girl has just turned 18, and is run off her feet at a wedding studio specializing in Chinese-Indonesian fusion style weddings. She always nails the perfect blend of the traditional Chinese *Heaven and Earth Worship* ritual and the Javanese water sprinkling rite. In her spare time, she loves scrolling through short videos to pick up nifty floral design ideas. On weekends, she never fails to drag her besties out for grilled skewers and iced tea. Her pocket notebook, decorated with dragon and phoenix batik embroidery patterns, is stuffed full of wedding candy wrappers.

As a researcher at the Malaysian Institute of Marine Research, she often stays up late analyzing coral data. She records parameters while working with samples every day, so her cuffs are frequently stained with salty seawater. After work, she simmers nasi lemak, and on weekends she always meets up with long-time colleagues to play mahjong. Her fingers are slightly stiff from years of handling tweezers when she lays mahjong tiles, yet she always hums upbeat Malay folk songs the whole time.

He is a young Filipino and a rookie surgeon who has just entered the profession. A fountain pen always peeks halfway out of his pocket. When suturing wounds, he will subconsciously hum the hymns he learned as a child. In his spare time, he likes to ask friends out to play local Filipino poker, and he also loves collecting festive sequined costume masks.

She is a 26-year-old Ecuadorian girl, with stubborn flower mud stains on the backs of her hands that never wash off completely. She spends most of her days crouched in the greenhouse filled with the scent of Andean herbs and tropical flowers, tending to succulents. Even on stormy days, she stays by the greenhouse trellises to protect the seedlings. After work, she huddles on a small stool beside the greenhouse scrolling through funny short videos, and occasionally joins her neighbors for a couple of rounds of poker.

Working in a foreign trade office building in Urumqi, she liaises with Central Asian clients and has amassed a huge fan base. After work, she loves to meet up with her besties for red willow lamb skewers, always tucks milk curds in her bag as energy bars, and plays the dombra to unwind on weekends.

She has worked at a home appliance customer service center in Seoul for two decades. Whenever she answers a call, she unconsciously leans slightly forward and softens her tone, apologizing with a smile over and over even when it is not her fault at all. After work, she loves playing hwatu (Korean flower cards) with her colleagues. At night, she curls up on the warm ondol heated floor binging those lengthy Korean family dramas. She always tucks a small pack of diced kimchi pickled by her mother-in-law in her pocket as a snack.

This girl can always be found sitting behind the checkout counter of a convenience store at the entrance of an old alley in Tehran. When ringing up purchases, her fingertips are always dusted with crumbs of Persian date cake. During breaks, she curls up in the corner scrolling through funny short videos in Turkic. Occasionally she makes plans to play Okey with her fellow townsfolk, and she has been saving up to go on a pilgrimage to the holy city of Qom once she has enough money.

The 22-year-old guy is an esports player. He spends most of his time in the training room covered with ice hockey posters, and all he does when he wins is scratch his head and grin sheepishly. During breaks, he loves playing Texas Hold 'em with his teammates, and he always touches the ice hockey sticker at the corner of his mouse pad before every match.

The 22-year-old researcher spends most of their time around kimchi samples at Seoul National University's fermentation lab, with their notebooks often mixed with technical terms written in Chinese characters. After work, they love ducking into the street food stall at the alley entrance to devour grilled skewers paired with soju. When writing up records, they can never resist tapping the desk to the beat of K-pop, and there is always homemade pickled bellflower root kimchi tucked in their pockets.

A 27-year-old woman from the Republic of the Congo runs a tiny nail salon by the Congo River. She excels at painting the bright, vivid geometric patterns and rainforest totems of Sapeur fashion on nail surfaces. She always polishes all her tools until they gleam brightly before calling it a day. In her free time, she loves scrolling through short nail art tutorial videos and binging jungle-themed TV series.

A 28-year-old cleaner works at a Haussmann-style office building in Paris. If anyone finds fault with her cleaning, she will squat there scrubbing repeatedly until the floor is so glossy that it reflects the overhead lights. After work, she always pops into the tiny bistro at the alley entrance, sipping affordable table wine while playing cards with her co-workers, and never reneges on her bets when she loses.

She is 32 years old, working as an assembler on the assembly line of an auto parts factory. Her ten fingers are covered with fine calluses. She is a person of few words in daily life and rarely joins her co-workers for card games. During breaks, she always clutches a paint-peeling enamel mug to steep aged tea. When she has spare time, she watches short daily dramas focusing on trivial family and neighborhood matters, leading a quiet, plain and steady life.

A 78-year-old retired technician lives in an old Gothic house with a pointed spire. He always sits perfectly straight and is punctual to a fault. Every Wednesday without fail, he arrives at the community pub right on schedule for a pint of freshly brewed beer. Once he finishes his drink, he joins his old buddies at a table for a game of cards. He never gets annoyed even when he loses, always smiling as he twists the loose thread on his cuff.

The 24-year-old photographer always slings his old camera over his shoulder, wandering through the old villages of Benin to document surviving folk cultural heritage. In his spare time, he loves collecting mini bronze pendants, and often squats at the village entrance to join the elders for poker games. He is well-liked wherever he goes.

As a 32-year-old surgeon, working round the clock in the operating room is the norm for him. After work, he enjoys brewing a pot of aged tea, and meets up with his mahjong buddies every week to play a couple of rounds. He never fails to feel for the mints in his pocket before every surgery.

A 24-year-old woman works as a professional organizer in a residential neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro. Her fingertips are always smudged with a little cardboard dust. She is used to reaching for high storage shelves with the nimble moves she learned from capoeira, unconsciously hums samba tunes while sorting things, and always squats at the street corner to play cards with her neighbors after work.

He is a young man from Papua New Guinea. He tends to cassava and coconut saplings on the slopes at the edge of the rainforest all year round. He always clutches the hem of his shirt nervously when settling accounts. In his spare time, he gathers on the open ground of the tribe to play cards with his fellow tribespeople. He also has a private hobby of collecting fallen colorful feather ornaments off the masks for the Sing-Sing Festival.

A 33-year-old programmer has a stable job at a software company in Bangalore. He keeps a miniature Shiva statue on his desk, and brings his own lunch box packed with vegetarian curry to work every day. He brews masala chai punctually at 3 p.m. each afternoon, and always joins his neighbors to play cards to kill time on weekends.

The 35-year-old fisherman sets sail in his small wooden boat long before dawn, with sea mud crammed under his fingernails. After calling it a day, he always squats under the seaside awning to play cards with his fellow fishermen. Before every voyage, he never fails to touch the tiger cowrie amulet fastened to the boat's gunwale. In his free time, he often drops by the village entrance to stomp along to the drum beats of the traditional war dance. He loves the beverage brewed from kava powder wrapped in tapa cloth.

A 27-year-old young man works as a ride-hailing driver in Los Angeles. He abides by Puritan-style frugality and American individualism: he can't bring himself to turn on the air conditioner in summer, and always digs out all the change stuck in the crevices of his car seats after his shift, not letting even a single penny slip through his fingers. He plays Texas Hold'em at the community garage every week, and often gets so absorbed in scrolling through short videos of Hollywood gossip that he forgets to accept ride orders.

The 81-year-old granny has thin calluses on the backs of her hands from decades of household toil. After retirement, she spends nearly all her time in her sun-dappled tiny kitchen, baking flatbreads that blend Inca quinoa and Spanish spices, and always makes two extra portions to share with her neighbors. Every Wednesday, without fail, she heads to the community square to play cards. When she binges local soap operas and comes across absurdly melodramatic plot twists, she even dabs at her tears with crumbly, lint-shedding tissues.

The 19-year-old lad spends most of the year poling a boat and casting fishing nets by the river in northern Yunnan. After hauling in the nets, he would always squat on the bank to play a couple of rounds of poker with his fellow workers. In his free time, he scrolls through short videos of the Torch Festival in his hometown to amuse himself.

A 55-year-old surgeon with 30 years of practice, he is decisive at work. His incisions are steady and precise, and he rarely makes mistakes. When off duty, he always takes his morin khuur (horsehead fiddle) to the grassland to play a few pieces. Occasionally, he also meets up with old friends from the same hospital to enjoy grilled skewers and kumis (fermented mare's milk).

In front of the floor-to-ceiling window of an office building in downtown Tokyo, she types away at her keyboard, her gaze fixed on a screen full of Chinese-Japanese bilingual financial reports. She barely speaks during meetings, but the views she shares are always precise and incisive.
As soon as she gets off work, she curls up at home binge-watching short clips of heartwarming healing anime. She always keeps salted senbei stocked in her desk drawer, and the Inari Omamori she prayed for last year sits perched at the corner of her desk.

This 52-year-old Mexican auntie has faint calluses on her palms from years of gripping barbells. She teaches fitness classes at a small community gym, always reminding her students with a smile, "Follow your breath, stretch just like a corn stalk that's soaked up plenty of rainwater." After class, she squats by the doorway scrolling through local funny short videos, munching on tortilla chips washed down with an ice-cold beer.

She is a 33-year-old high-speed train attendant. Shuttling through the carriages every day, she helps passengers stow their luggage and reminds them when their stops are approaching. A small Xilan Kapu (traditional Tujia brocade) sachet woven by her mother is always tucked in her pocket. When off duty, she loves binge-watching family ethics dramas, and on weekends she gets together with friends to play mahjong. Whenever she loses a game, she scratches her head and grins sheepishly.

The 19-year-old girl from southern Brazil works as a loom operator at a textile mill. After work, she often gathers with her workmates to play cards. She binges Portuguese-language soap operas in her free time, and always quietly leaves bread crumbs for the stray cats hanging around the factory gate.

He is a 27-year-old plumber and electrician who has settled in the Philippines. His fingertips are perpetually stained with rust marks that can never be fully wiped clean. When he goes from home to home in Chinatown doing plumbing and electrical repairs, he gives straightforward quotes and never haggles over trivial matters. After calling it a day, he always squats at the alley entrance to play a couple of rounds of poker with his fellow townsmen.

The 33-year-old nurse, who grew up in mountain tower villages since childhood, is run off her feet at Grozny Community Hospital. Right after getting off work, she always drags her colleagues out for grilled skewers and kvass. She saves up to collect ancient Caucasian silver jewelry. She always hums hometown folk tunes when changing IV drips for patients, speaking to them in a soft and gentle voice, yet she is extremely picky about the minimum-spend coupons at the skewer shop.

A 23-year-old young tour guide always explains the spots in a soft, gentle voice when taking tourists around Shinto shrines, ancient streets and popular anime check-in spots on workdays. After work, he loves popping into izakayas to wash down yakitori with ice-cold beer. When he has free time, he simply cozies up in his rented apartment to catch up on old anime series.

The 32-year-old man is the CEO of a tech firm based in Tokyo. On workdays, he calls the shots on all projects in his solid wood office adorned with seasonal flower arrangements, and is known for his decisive work style. In his spare time, he enjoys brewing matcha, and on weekends he occasionally invites his subordinates to izakayas for yakitori skewers and a casual drink.

The 29-year-old CEO of a startup keeps a Manchu calligraphy scroll inherited from his grandfather hanging in his office. Swamped with financing negotiations all workday long, he is a resolute decision-maker. Off work, his favorite thing to do is meet up with his childhood buddies for grilled skewers and iced beer every Friday. When eating the skewers, he always sorts the skewer sticks by length, calling it a little obsession of his that stems from the battle formations of the Eight Banners.

The 77-year-old granny has thin calluses on both hands, left from making butter sculptures and herding cattle and sheep in her younger years. After retirement, she walks along the circumambulation path every day spinning a brass prayer wheel. Her favorite pastime is playing Tibetan-style poker with her old girlfriends. Whenever she loses, she will make fruit-flavored butter tea with a recipe she learned from short videos — she always loses on purpose just to cheer everyone up.

The 48-year-old man always huddles over his coconut wood desk sorting out tribal legends, with the sweet scent of coconut permeating every line of the texts. In his spare time, he either practices a session of fire knife dance, or rounds up neighbors to play local coconut cards.

A 51-year-old Brazilian real estate agent always paces back and forth in his agency office clutching a leather-bound property listings book. When promoting properties on the edge of the rainforest, he always reminds people not to touch the old ferns, saying they are the homes of forest spirits. After work, he loves heading to the neighborhood bar for grilled skewers. He keeps half a box of rainforest feathers tucked away in his drawer, and rubs them whenever he feels anxious.

She is a senior civil servant responsible for civil registration at the city hall. In her daily work, she always patiently helps local residents sort out their application materials, and is meticulous and considerate in everything she does. After work, she loves experimenting with Mediterranean-style stews, and often arranges to play bridge with her long-time neighbors on weekends, living a truly laid-back and peaceful life.

A 60-year-old Colombian porter has been hauling burlap sacks in coffee storage areas for 30 years, yet he still keeps his back perfectly straight. The calluses on his palms are so thick that they can grind down the burrs on hemp ropes. After work, he always squats on the street corner playing cards with his fellow workers, and loves humming Cumbia tunes.

This 80-year-old retiree always sits in the rocking chair on his front porch soaking up the warm sun. He never misses the weekly bridge game at the community activity room every Wednesday. On his free days, blues melodies drift constantly out of his worn, paint-chipped old radio. Occasionally, he rubs the old scar on his knuckles as he recounts tiny bits of old stories from the civil rights marches he joined. He always keeps mints in his pocket to hand out to the neighborhood kids.

After retiring, she always carries her rattan chair to the balcony and stays there, sipping brewed yerba mate while watching live sports broadcasts. In the afternoons, she plays bridge with her old gal pals at the community activity center. Even if she loses the game, she just rubs her grass-scented fingertips, and her only little wish is to bask in the sun a bit longer on sunny days.

She is a 38-year-old worker at a food processing plant in Rotterdam, her fingertips perpetually smudged with pale yellow grease from work. During break times, she always ropes her coworkers into playing poker for small snacks. Once off shift, she slings her old, worn camera over her shoulder and heads to the canal banks to photograph the sunset shadows of windmills and tulips.

She is a 32-year-old woman from Botswana, exceptionally quick and deft at wiping tables, setting out tableware and greeting guests. After work, she always loves curling up in the staff dorm scrolling through local short videos. On her days off, she would invite fellow townsfolk to get together for card games. Whenever customers leave their belongings behind, she always keeps them carefully and waits for the owners to come and claim them.

A 21-year-old Brazilian photographer roams the streets and alleyways of Rio de Janeiro with a camera slung over his shoulder, capturing the vivid, dynamic moments of samba dancers and capoeira performers. After wrapping up his day's work, he loves ducking into old local taverns for grilled skewers and cachaça. Lemon hard candies are always tucked in his pockets, and he will slip one to anyone who strikes his fancy.

I work as a cashier at a neighborhood grocery store that's been in business for 30 years in Kyoto's Shitamachi. When tallying up bills, my fingertips always subconsciously tap the counter three times. On my days off, I either attend ikebana lessons at a public class near my home, or meet up with long-time neighbors to play hanafuda.

In a tiny noodle shop tucked away in the old alleys of Amsterdam, this 60-year-old man has hands thick with calluses from kneading dough. After finishing work each day, he always squats at the alley entrance to play poker with his old buddies. He loves iced rum, and always hums Caribbean tunes while kneading dough.

This 60-year-old female CEO from Benin always keeps a Dahomey bronze relief paperweight in her office and speaks in a soft, gentle tone. After work, there is nothing she enjoys more than playing local card games with her long-time gal pals. When binge-watching TV series, she constantly pops dates into her mouth, and when lost in thought, she has a habit of rubbing the bronze ring passed down to her from her mother.

She is a 23-year-old handicraft vendor from Nigeria. Every day, she stands behind the counter draped in Aso Oke fabric, explaining the Orisha myths featured in bronze carvings to her customers. After work, she always cozies up in her rented apartment scrolling through edited short clips of oral epics from her hometown. She is exceptionally patient and thoughtful in everything she does.

A 27-year-old female teacher teaches ethnic history at a school on the edge of the grasslands. During lessons, she always spreads a small flannel blanket embroidered with yurt patterns on the podium. Occasionally, her fingertips brush against the dombra strings, and she would hum a few snippets of epic poetry. After class, she loves curling up in her own yurt to binge-watch domestic Chinese costume dramas more than anything else, and she never forgets to tuck two lip balms in her bag.

The 60-year-old American architect specializes in community-focused architecture. His designs feature hollowed-out windows carved with corn grain patterns and textures inspired by woven silver ornaments, which implicitly echo the animist belief that all things have souls and embody his deep-seated obsession with cultural revitalization. He never misses his Friday night ritual: hunkering down in the garage with his old neighbors, sipping iced beer and watching baseball games.

As a grassroots civil servant in Haiti, she often braves the sweltering tropical heat and humidity to go around neighborhoods addressing local people's appeals and concerns. In her free time, she meets up with her long-time female friends to play local card games and chat in Haitian Creole, and occasionally sorts out small Voodoo-related folk trinkets.

This is a bank teller who has worked at a street-side bank in Kinshasa for 30 years. She speaks in a soft, gentle voice, always humming old-school rumba tunes when counting francs. After work, she loves scrolling through short videos of local stews, and meets up with her old colleagues at a teahouse to play cards every Friday.

At 34, he works in a tiny foreign trade cubicle near the China-Russia border, handling orders by switching back and forth between Turkic languages and Russian. When clients make things difficult for him, he just presses his lips tight and nods, and he always hands over documents with both hands. Every Saturday without fail, he goes fishing in the suburbs, and he is also fond of collecting vintage Turkic language cassette tapes.

The girl has just turned 19, working as a pet groomer at the pet shop right at the alley entrance. Her work stool is padded with scrap pieces of Xilan Kapu, the traditional Tujia brocade hand-woven by her grandmother. She always adjusts the pets' grooming styles over and over again to meet customers' requirements, afraid of upsetting them in the slightest. After work, she cozies up in the tiny cubicle she rents in a stilt house, scrolling through short videos of adorable pets. On weekends, she always heads to the community square to practice Baishou Dance, the traditional Tujia hand-swaying dance, with local grannies.

This 64-year-old veteran programmer has been coding for four decades. He is accustomed to sorting out all bugs with minimalist logic. When he has free time, he slings a fishing rod over his shoulder and spends half a day lingering by the lakeshore on the outskirts of the city. Every Midsummer Festival, he volunteers to help the community build the wooden frames for the celebration.

She spends all day showing properties to clients. At the real estate agency in Accra's old town, she always keeps her kente-cloth-bound notebook close at hand, and makes a point of verifying water and electricity billing details ahead of time for every work task. Once off work, she curls up in her rented apartment binge-watching local family dramas.

A 41-year-old carpenter, whose knuckles are perpetually stained with wood shavings and sawdust, always hunkers down with hunched shoulders to work in the wooden shed beside the yurts on the grassland. In his free time, he either crouches in the corner of the shed to play a few rounds of poker with his fellow townsmen, or hums snippets of ancient epics while stroking his well-worn old dombra.

A 29-year-old female lawyer works at a small law firm alongside Amsterdam's canals. She abides by the pragmatic and rigorous tenets of Protestantism, and never accepts any gifts from clients when handling cases — she would even politely turn down a simple offer of hot coffee. After work, she curls up in her attic scrolling through nautical-themed short videos. On weekends, she often meets up with her bridge buddies for games, and her fingertips always unconsciously stroke the dried tulip left by her grandmother, which she keeps in her pocket, as she lays down her cards.

A 32-year-old Malaysian flight attendant always helps her junior crew colleagues carry supplies and cover shifts when working on flights. On her rotating days off, she invites fellow townsfolk to get together for poker games. Before going to bed, she often scrolls through a few short videos of traditional South Asian singing and dancing to unwind.

The young man has just turned 23. He works as a programmer at a small studio in Lima, and always delves into new programming frameworks. He has a habit of nibbling the hangnails on his fingertips when typing, and his favorite thing to do after work is rounding up his friends to play dominoes at seaside skewer joints.

A 24-year-old woman works in an arcade studio tucked away in an old alley in Jakarta. An old radio beside her plays gamelan tunes on loop. She spends most of her time tracing wayang kulit (shadow puppet) figures on batik fabrics, her fingertips permanently stained with indelible paint.
When she gets so immersed in painting that she loses track of everything else, she unconsciously nibbles her lower lip. In her free time, she loves squatting at the doorway playing dominoes with neighbors. Whenever she loses, she hands over a freshly painted tiny shadow puppet as the stake, and never feels upset about the loss.

At 39, he is a civil servant at the city hall. Wielding examination and approval authority, he always lines his pockets on the sly. After work, he loves nothing more than heading to a small tavern in the old alley to play poker with acquaintances, and always resorts to petty tricks to win his pals' prized reserved red wine.

This 74-year-old woman comes from Ethiopia. Before her retirement, she helped handle affairs of the age sets under the community's Gadaa system.
Now she spends her days tending to several old yellow cattle in her small courtyard, and she always loves rubbing the soft fuzz at the base of the cows' ears. Her favorite pastime is carrying a low stool to play cards with her neighbors; even when she loses, she slaps her thigh and laughs heartily. She always scrolls through short pastoral song videos before going to bed, with tiny crumbs of chewed frankincense often lingering at the corner of her mouth.

This is the 54-year-old cleaning auntie of our community. She always works a beat slower when wiping the corridor handrails, often stares out the window in a daze, and occasionally faint images of the buzkashi field flit through her mind. After dinner, she loves gathering with her old sisters to play Shengji, a popular Chinese trick-taking card game. She takes her time playing each card but never plays foul. Whenever she wins, she pulls out milk curds to share with the whole group.
A 20-year-old young man always goes live to share folk culture in his small rented apartment decorated with woven tapestries, and playing poker is his favorite pastime when he is free.

The 25-year-old is a resident singer at a speakeasy, who always blends vintage blues tunes and hip-hop beats into his songwriting. In his spare time, he loves nothing more than rounding up his buddies for card games, and he also often visits the church choir for creative inspiration.

This 29-year-old researcher spends nearly all his workdays holed up in the ancient texts archive sorting out cultural heritage of the Turkic steppe, so his fingertips are always smudged with faint ink marks from old paper. In his spare time, he loves brewing flower and fruit tea, and often scrolls through short videos about the daily lives of Central Asian herders.
